messages:
Maria (support): Hey team — customer ACME Inc reports p95 spikes on generate API since ~09:10 UTC. Multiple calls showing timeouts and a lot of 503s. They're on Dedicated region-us-west-2. Opening thread to triage.

Samir (eng-oncall): Seen the PagerDuty alert. Grafana shows p95 went from ~180ms to ~1.2s starting 09:08. Errors are primarily 502/503 from the front proxy. Queue length on gateway spiked. Any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: service/inference-gateway v1.42.0 -> v1.43.0 by @leo at 2026-03-15T09:05:12Z :white_check_mark:

Leo (eng-runtime): That deploy touched admission control defaults (concurrency limit) to add per-tenant conservative limits. It should lower concurrency, not raise latency. I'm pulling traces.

Anya (eng-sre): I'm seeing large backlog on worker pods: inflight_tokens=3500, queue_depth=58k for model-redwood/ggml-small-8bit. Pod CPU is 95%, GPU util ~98% on a subset of nodes. Looks like hot shard problem.

Maria (support): Customer says their traffic pattern had a brief burst (integration test loop) but within normal SLAs historically.

Samir (eng-oncall): Repro plan: if gateway is admitting bursts but worker-side scheduling is slow (long per-request tail due to context length or KV cache misses) we get head-of-line blocking. Can someone check per-request latency distribution at worker level? Also check admission reject rate.

Leo (eng-runtime): Worker-level p99 shows long tails — some requests hitting 9s CPU time (large input), but median still ~150ms. Admission rejects increased from 0 to ~25% as of 09:11.

Anya (eng-sre): Also noticing connection backlog at nginx front proxy: accept queue spikes, backlog_sockets ~1200. Kernel drops reported. Looks like TCP queueing before we even proxy to gateway.

Maria (support): Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they want traffic stable. Can we implement a quick fallback for them to a smaller model or enable dedicated burst capacity?

Samir (eng-oncall): Short-term mitigations we can do now:
- Increase gateway admission-control token-bucket refill to allow more concurrency for this tenant (risk: overload workers)
- Route ACME traffic to fallback model (smaller LLM) with lower per-request CPU
- Temporarily spin up more worker nodes and mark them to serve that tenant only
- Adjust nginx backlog and kernel tunables (net.core.somaxconn) — short-lived but helps accept queue

Leo (eng-runtime): I can flip a routing rule to send ACME to model-redwood/quant-2x. It reduces latency massively. Will push in 2m. Anyone comfortable with that immediate risk?

Anya (eng-sre): I'll scale worker pool + set autoscaler override. Adding 6 nodes now. Also increasing somaxconn and tcp_max_syn_backlog on the affected nodes.

Maria (support): Noted. I'll tell the customer we have a mitigation path and will enable fallback; asking if they accept temporary reduced model fidelity.

Customer (via support DM): "We prefer stable performance over perfect quality. Please switch us to fallback if it helps. Thanks."

Samir (eng-oncall): Ok executing plan: Leo, route change. Anya, scale. I'll watch metrics and dial admission control if worker load flares.

Leo (eng-runtime): Patch applied — routing rule created: if tenant==acme -> model=quant-2x, ttl=30m. Command:
```
# routing apply
rctl set-route --tenant acme --model redwood/quant-2x --priority 10 --ttl 1800
```

deploy-bot: route apply accepted by control-plane (req_id=XYZ-123)

Anya (eng-sre): Nodes requested, new nodes provisioning (EC2 spot/ondemand mix). Overrode HPA target to 70% for worker pods. Also ran:
```
sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=4096
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048
```

Samir (eng-oncall): Observing metrics: within 3m, gateway queue depth down from 58k -> 2.1k. p95 dropped to ~320ms, p99 to ~980ms. Worker CPU still high but stabilizing. Error rate dropped to <1%.

Maria (support): Customer confirmed traffic is stable and 503s stopped. They reported p95 acceptable.

Anya (eng-sre): Follow-ups: need to identify root cause of hot shard. Early hypothesis: tenant routing affinity caused disproportionate placement on subset of GPU nodes. Also new concurrent long requests (integration tests with big context) triggered KV cache pressure, causing slower generation and more blocking.

Leo (eng-runtime): I'll dig into placement algorithm and kernel queueing. Might need to change our per-tenant spread to reduce affinity and better balance KV cache state.

Samir (eng-oncall): Short-term action items (owner):
- Leo: investigate placement and admission control interaction; produce reproducible test by EOD. (owner: Leo)
- Anya: check node packing policy and add better anti-affinity for heavy tenants; submit infra PR. (owner: Anya)
- Maria: confirm with ACME about test patterns and request logs; collect example payloads. (owner: Maria)
- Samir: update runbook with these mitigation steps and add checklist for per-tenant fallback. (owner: Samir)

Maria (support): Logged customer follow-up. They provided payload samples — big context + multiple stop tokens. Uploading to S3: s3://redwood-support/acme/2026-03-15/payloads

Leo (eng-runtime): Quick repro steps I recommend for test infra:
1) replay sample payloads against a single worker pool with constrained nodes
2) measure KV cache hit rate and per-token CPU
3) vary admission concurrency and observe head-of-line impact

Samir (eng-oncall): Also adding throttling option to gateway to prefer rejects over unbounded queue to avoid tail amplification. Will prototype a config toggle: `admission.reject_on_queue_overflow=true`.

Anya (eng-sre): Long-term: autoscaler policy should be sensitive to queue depth and not just CPU. HPA -> custom metrics (queue_depth, kv_cache_misses). I'll add a spike-scaler.

Maria (support): Customer thanked us. Planning a follow-up call tomorrow with engineering to discuss long-term protections.

Samir (eng-oncall): Closing notes: immediate mitigation worked (fallback + scale + kernel tweaks). Root cause candidate: tenant placement affinity + bursty large-context requests causing KV cache churn and long tails -> head-of-line queueing. Will keep thread open until postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0421 (priority: high) — linked to account ACME Inc.

Maria (support): Adding ticket link to customer message. I'll attach metrics screenshots and the payload S3 URL.

Leo (eng-runtime): Starting a repro job now on test cluster. Will update thread with logs.

Anya (eng-sre): PR opened for HPA change: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/1427

Samir (eng-oncall): Thanks all. I'll run the postmortem template tomorrow and assign follow-ups. :thumbsup:
